profile_text.body:
OpenAI is a for-profit AI company founded in 2015 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. Its primary public-facing product is ChatGPT, described on its website as a tool to answer questions, write, create images, complete work, and code, with the site noting that chats may be reviewed and used to improve its AI models. The company also offers the OpenAI API giving developers access to its GPT models on a usage-based basis, along with an associated Playground and Dashboard for testing, fine-tuning, and team management.

Beyond ChatGPT, OpenAI tracks several other products: DALL-E for image generation, Sora for video generation, the Whisper API for speech recognition and transcription, and Operator, an autonomous web agent capable of browser control. These products span chat, coding tools, image and video generation, and voice and audio categories, reflecting a broad position across current AI application areas.

OpenAI carries substantial legal exposure, with cases filed across multiple federal courts. Matters include suits in the Northern District of California such as Starr v. OpenAI Group PBC, Craddock v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, and Byrd v. OpenAI, Inc., copyright-related litigation in the Southern District of New York brought by wikiHow, Inc., cases in the Northern and Southern Districts of Florida, a Hawaii district court action, an appellate matter at the Ninth Circuit involving X.AI Corp., and two federal government actions styled United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC filed in the Eastern District of Arkansas. The site's held facts indicate the heaviest concentration of legal exposure is associated with California, with 181 matters recorded under that jurisdiction.
